statement.p: Below is the graph of the derivative f'(x) of a function defined on the interval (0,8). You can click on the graph to see a larger version in a separate window.

image.shortdescription: Graph of the derivative of a function f

description.p: The derivative function f'(x) is below the x-axis on the intervals (0,3)\cup(5,8) and above the x-axis on the interval (3,5).
It is decreasing on the intervals (0,2)\cup(4,6) and increasing on the intervals (2,4)\cup(6,8).
It has local minimums at x=2 and x=6, and it has a local maximum at x=4.

statement.p: Refer to the graph to answer each of the following questions. For parts (A) and (B), use interval notation to report your answer. (If needed, you use U for the union symbol.)
(A) For what values of x in (0,8) is f(x) increasing? (If the function is not increasing anywhere, enter None .)
(B) For what values of x in (0,8) is f(x) concave down? (If the function is not concave down anywhere, enter None .)
(C) Find all values of x in (0,8) is where f(x) has a local minimum, and list them (separated by commas) in the box below. (If there are no local minima, enter None .)
(D) Find all values of x in (0,8) is where f(x) has an inflection point, and list them (separated by commas) in the box below. (If there are no inflection points, enter None .)

solution.p: (A) The function f(x) is increasing in the intervals where f'(x) \ge 0 : (3,5)
(B) The function f(x) is concave down in the intervals where f' is decreasing: (0,2)\cup(4,6).
(C) The function f(x) has a local minimum at those values of x where f'(x) =0 and f' is negative to the left and positive to the right. There is only one such value: x = 3
(D) The function f(x) has an inflection point at those values of x at which the derivative has a local maximum or a local minimum: x = 2,4,6
